summary: Fan out rule-observer agents over game traces, dedupe by ruleId, adversarially verify each unique finding.

confirmed.violation: Rule 583.3 requires that when a triggered ability's condition is met, it 'behaves like an Activated Ability and is placed on the Chain'. The engine places `play-spell` triggers on the chain correctly, but `play-self` triggers resolve immediately without ever being placed on the chain, so the opponent never receives the 577.3.c.1 response window.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts:273 (chainActive gate → inline executeEffect at :302-335); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:418 (playUnit fires play-self without opening a chain; contrast playSpell addToChain at :783)
confirmed.notes:
Rule 583.3 states unconditionally that a triggered ability "is placed on the Chain" (583.3.a: during Closed OR Open states). The engine violates this for play-self triggers on units.

Mechanism: fireTriggers() gates chain placement on `ctx.draft.interaction?.chain?.active === true` (trigger-runner.ts:273). When true it calls addToChain (rule-compliant); when false it falls through to executeEffect() inline (lines 302-335), never opening a chain and never giving the opponent the 577.3.c.1 response window. The code comment at :270-272 miscites rule 541 as justification — 541 only says triggers during an active chain join THAT chain; it does not license inline resolution when no chain is active.

playUnit reducer (cards.ts:401-432) never calls addToChain/createInteractionState before fireTriggers({type:"play-self"}) at :418, so chainActive is false and the trigger resolves immediately. playSpell (cards.ts:783) DOES addToChain the spell first, so chainActive is true when fireTriggers({type:"play-spell"}) runs at :792 — hence the observed asymmetry (play-spell triggers go on chain, play-self do not).

Trace verified in do_not_commit/wf-traces/game-wf-4.jsonl: seq=22 chosen=playUnit ogn-051-298, post state.interaction.chain=null; seq=23 available=[endTurn, concede, playUnit] for player-2 — no chain item, no target prompt, no player-1 priority. seq=163 chosen=playUnit ogn-044-298, post hand contains freshly-drawn ogn-059-298 and interaction.chain=None — the "draw 1" trigger executed inside the same reducer. Card texts confirmed as play-self triggered abilities (solari-shieldbearer.ts:13, clockwork-keeper.ts:13-14; abilities are parsed from rulesText).

confirmed.violation: Rule 550.1: for a Showdown that is part of Combat, the Attacking and Defending players are the Relevant Players. The engine sets `defendingPlayer` to the same value as `attackingPlayer` (the player who invoked startShowdown) instead of the battlefield's controller, so `relevantPlayers` contains only the attacker. The real defender is excluded from every combat-showdown priority window and never receives Focus.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:818-835 (startShowdown reducer; buggy form at c05e29a^, fixed in c05e29a)
confirmed.notes: Rule 550.1 text confirmed: combat-showdown Relevant Players = Attacking + Defending. Trace game-wf-3.jsonl seq 127/129/131 (and 287/289) shows showdown {attackingPlayer:"player-2", defendingPlayer:"player-2", relevantPlayers:["player-2"], isCombatShowdown:true} while battlefields["player-2-bf-ogn-275-298"].controller="player-1" — defender player-1 excluded, single passShowdownFocus closes each showdown. Root cause in the pre-c05e29a startShowdown reducer: relevantPlayers was built as [playerId, ...(contestedBy !== playerId ? [contestedBy] : [])] and defender was `uniqueRelevant.find(p => p !== playerId) ?? playerId` — bf.controller was never consulted, so when the invoker == contestedBy (the normal case), defender collapsed to the attacker. Trace mtime 18:05Z predates fix commit c05e29a (18:18Z, "showdown defendingPlayer/relevantPlayers per rule 550"), so the violation is real for the engine that produced these traces; current HEAD is already patched.

The engine models startShowdown as an optional discretionary move offered in parallel with resolveFullCombat, so a player can resolve combat without ever entering the mandatory Showdown sub-phase.

confirmed.violation: Rule 540.4.b: the chain ends only when all Relevant Players have passed once IN SEQUENCE (i.e., consecutively with no intervening action). Taking a non-pass action must reset the pass tracking. The engine does not clear `passedPlayers` when a player takes the `counterSpell` action, so a stale earlier pass counts toward the sequence and the chain resolves without the other player regaining priority.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:1028-1041 (counterSpell reducer does not reset chain.passedPlayers / activePlayer); cf. packages/riftbound-engine/src/chain/chain-state.ts:236 where addToChain does reset it.
confirmed.notes: Rule text: 540.4.b says the chain ends when all Relevant Players have "passed once in sequence" — the in-sequence wording supports the claim that an intervening non-pass action must break the pass streak. Source: the counterSpell reducer (chain-moves.ts:1028-1041) only flips `countered=true` on the target item; it touches neither `chain.passedPlayers` nor `chain.activePlayer`. Contrast addToChain (chain-state.ts:236) which explicitly resets `passedPlayers: []`. Trace: seq=123 post-state passedPlayers=['player-1'] activePlayer=player-2; seq=124 chosen=counterSpell(player-2), post-state passedPlayers still ['player-1'] activePlayer still player-2; seq=125 chain=null — player-1 never regained priority after player-2 acted. Same at seq=94→96. Caveat: rule 601.2 classifies Counter as a Limited Action invokable only "when directed to by Game Effects", not a rule-540 discretionary choice, and the engine's own comment (chain-moves.ts:1026-1027) says counterSpell is "for sandbox/effect-executor use only" with no enumerator — so an alternative framing is that the deeper bug is counterSpell being offered as a selectable priority action at all. Either way, the observable state violates 540.4.b exactly as claimed: a stale pass survives a non-pass action and the chain resolves without the opponent's post-action priority window.

The claim misclassifies `counterSpell` as "a spell or activated ability played during a chain" that 540.1.b requires to be added as a chain item. The rules say otherwise:

- Rule 601 defines **Counter** as a *Game Action* (a Limited Action, 601.2), formatted as "Counter [a card or ability on the chain]" (601.3). Players may only Counter "when directed to by Game Effects" (601.2.a). Game Actions are not spells (533.1) or abilities (533.2) and do not themselves become chain items.
- Rule 540.1.b ("The spell will be added to the chain, following the steps of playing a card") governs *playing a spell card*. The card whose text reads "Counter …" is what goes on the chain — via `playSpell`, which the engine does add as a chain item — and opponents get their 542 priority loop before it resolves. When that card resolves under 543.1, its effect executes the Counter action, which correctly just marks the target `countered:true` (effect-executor.ts:632-648). No new chain item is required or expected for the Counter action itself.

Engine intent matches this reading: chain-moves.ts:1026-1027 — "Rule 601: Counter is a card effect, not a player Discretionary Action. No enumerator — this move exists for sandbox/effect-executor use only." The tracer explicitly blacklists it from selection (game-tracer.ts:85 `NEVER_PICK` includes `"counterSpell"`).

Either way, the observed behavior — Counter action mutating in place without becoming a chain item — is rules-correct under 601. The 540.1.b / 563.2.a reaction window attaches to the *card that grants Counter*, not to the Counter action, and that path (playSpell → chain item → priority → resolve → effect-executor `counter`) is implemented.

If there is a real issue here, it is 601.2.a (counterSpell should not be player-enumerable at all), not 540.1.b — but that is a different claim, and the code already documents it as sandbox-only with no enumerator.
